brief: A global bond selloff extended after US and Eurozone flash PMIs beat expectations (US composite at a 5-year high of 58.4 vs 55.3 expected, Eurozone composite at a 3-year high of 53.1 vs 51.7 expected), signaling resilient growth that reinforces the case for continued Fed hiking. A rebound in Brent crude (+3.86% to $103.08) on doubts over a US-Iran deal added further hawkish pressure. Fed October hike odds rose from 53% Tuesday to 69% by Thursday's close, with this morning's futures pricing 71%. ECB October hike odds rose from 48% to 66%. Year-end Fed pricing now implies 37bps of additional hikes, a near-even chance of two more by December. The 10yr Treasury yield jumped 15.2bps to a post-2007 high of 5.11%, its biggest one-day move since Liberation Day in April 2025, and the 5yr yield rose above 5% for the first time since 2007. A weak $70bn 5yr auction tailed 3.1bps above the pre-sale yield. European yields also hit multi-year highs, and the Franco-German 10yr spread widened to 110.4bps, its highest since the 2012 euro crisis. Equities fell broadly (S&P 500 -0.75%, its biggest decline in a month) despite the strong growth data, with only energy stocks gaining.
